panels.title: Transaction Apply Failed Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions that fail during the apply (transactor) stage, per second — i.e. the transactor ran but the result was not tesSUCCESS.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of tx.transactor spans at the apply stage whose ter_result is not tesSUCCESS, over the dashboard rate interval, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady low background is normal (tefPAST_SEQ, tecUNFUNDED, etc.); the transactor legitimately rejects many transactions.*

###### Healthy range:
*A low, stable rate; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A sharp rise above baseline, which points to a submission pattern that is systematically failing at apply.*

###### Source:
[Transactor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/tx/detail/Transactor.cpp)

###### Function:
`Transactor::operator()`

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", span_name="tx.transactor", stage="apply", ter_result!~"tesSUCCESS|"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", "Failed / Sec", "", "")

panels.title: Transaction Processing Latency by Type
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 95th-percentile time to process a transaction, broken down by transaction type.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th-percentile of processing durations over 5 minutes, grouped by transaction type and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; compare types to find the expensive ones.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few milliseconds for simple payments; workload- and type-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A type whose latency climbs, pointing to expensive processing or resource pressure.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction`

panels.title: Transaction Rate by Type
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many transactions of each type enter processing per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second processing rate over 5 minutes, grouped by transaction type and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows the transaction mix; payments usually lead.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; mix reflects network activity.*

###### Watch for:
*A single type spiking far above baseline, consistent with a spam campaign of that type.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction`

panels.title: Transaction Results by Type
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The non-success result codes transactions return, by transaction type.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of failing transactions over 5 minutes, grouped by type and result code.*

###### Reading it:
*Fewer failures is better; use it to see which types fail and why.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; a modest background of expected failures is normal.*

###### Watch for:
*A surge of one failure code for one type, indicating a systemic issue or abusive submissions.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction`

panels.title: Transaction Receive vs Suppressed
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Raw transactions received from peers, split by whether they were duplicates suppressed before processing.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of received transactions over the window, split by suppressed flag and node.*

###### Reading it:
*A large suppressed share is normal, since the same transaction arrives from many peers.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; suppressed typically exceeds newly processed.*

###### Watch for:
*A collapse in suppression (duplicate filtering failing) or an overall receive flood.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

panels.title: Transaction Processing Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions entering the processing pipeline versus raw transactions arriving from peers.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rates of processed transactions and received peer transactions over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Received sits above processed; the difference is deduplicated relay traffic.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; both scale with network volume.*

###### Watch for:
*A receive rate spiking well above processing, consistent with relay flooding.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp) · [PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

panels.title: Transaction Path Distribution
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The split of transactions by origin: submitted locally versus relayed from peers.*

###### How it's computed:
*Processed-transaction rate over 5 minutes, split by local-origin flag and shown as proportions.*

###### Reading it:
*Most traffic on a network node is peer-relayed; local dominates on a submission node.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent on the node's role.*

###### Watch for:
*An unexpected surge in local submissions, consistent with a local client flooding the node.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::processTransaction`

panels.title: Transaction Processing Duration Heatmap
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The full distribution of transaction processing times over the window.*

###### How it's computed:
*Counts of transactions in each latency band per 5-minute window, shown as color density.*

###### Reading it:
*A tight low band is healthy; spread bands mean uneven processing time.*

###### Healthy range:
*Most mass in the low-latency bands; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A distinct slow cluster (multi-modal timing) hidden by percentile charts.*

[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

panels.title: TxQ Accept: Applied Ratio per Node (State Timeline)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The applied fraction of TxQ accepts per node over time: the share of queued transactions that were included in a ledger versus removed on failure.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per node, applied accepts divided by applied-plus-failed accepts over the window.*

###### Reading it:
*Green (>=90% applied) is a healthy drain; yellow is degraded; red means accepts are mostly failing.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or near 100% applied when the queue is draining healthily; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A node dropping into yellow or red, which signals queue pressure, under-bidding, or fee escalation on that node.*

###### Source:
[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)

###### Function:
`TxQ::accept`

*Lower is better; isolates which stage dominates processing time.*

*Each stage typically sub-millisecond to a few ms; workload-dependent.*

*One stage's latency rising, pinpointing the bottleneck in transaction handling.*

*The 95th-percentile time to apply the agreed transaction set into each new ledger.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; a major component of ledger build time.*

panels.title: TxQ Enqueue Rate by Transaction Type

*How many transactions are queued (rather than applied immediately) per second, by type.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of queue-enqueue operations over 5 minutes, grouped by transaction type and node.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows the demand mix hitting the queue and how it shifts as the queue fills.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; low or zero when the network is not congested.*

###### Watch for:
*A spam burst of one type, an early indicator of fee escalation.*

###### Source:
[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)

panels.title: Queue Bypass Ratio (Direct Apply vs Enqueue)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The fraction of transactions that applied straight to the open ledger instead of being queued.*

###### How it's computed:
*Direct-apply rate divided by direct-apply plus enqueue rate over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Higher is better; near 1.0 means the network is not congested.*

###### Healthy range:
*Close to 1.0 when not congested; falls as demand exceeds capacity.*

###### Watch for:
*A falling ratio, the cleanest single signal the network has entered sustained fee escalation.*

###### Source:
[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)

###### Function:
`TxQ::tryDirectApply ; TxQ::apply`

panels.title: Queue Cleanup Rate (Expired Entries)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often expired transactions are removed from the queue each ledger, per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of queue-cleanup operations over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Low is healthy; a rising rate means submitters are abandoning transactions.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near zero when not congested; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising rate, a demand-frustration signal where submitters under-bid the escalating fee and gave up.*

###### Source:
[TxQ.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/TxQ.cpp)
